title: OpenWork character card
description: Interchange contract for a character card OpenWork can import or export. A Character Card V2 envelope, plus the OpenWork vendor block under `data.extensions.openwork` that carries the adult-content flag, the opening scene, and the character's hard limits. Two rules this schema cannot express: a card file must be at most 2000000 bytes, and a card may also arrive embedded in an uncompressed PNG `tEXt` chunk keyed `chara`, base64-encoded, in which case this schema describes the decoded payload.

spec.description: A `chara_card_v3` card is accepted on import and narrowed to V2; the fields V3 adds and this app does not keep are reported to the user as losses rather than dropped silently. Export writes V2, and V3 alongside it in PNG.

additionalProperties.description: Ignored. Nothing outside `data` is read, so a card that sets a top-level `nsfw` or `sceneRecords` is setting nothing.

mes_example.description: Exchanges separated by `<START>`. `{{char}}` and `{{user}}` expand at compile time.

system_prompt.description: Replaces the app default. `{{original}}` recovers it.

post_history_instructions.description: Preserved on export and never compiled into a prompt. The engine appends the per-turn system string before all chat history, so a field whose entire meaning is that it lands after history cannot be honoured. Absent and reported beats present and misplaced.

extensions.description: Vendor data. Only the `openwork` namespace is kept on import; every other namespace is removed, and the removal is reported to the user rather than done silently. A card is a stranger's file, and an unknown vendor block is text that would otherwise ride into the app unread.

noPrivilegeKeys.description: A card may not carry engine-privilege keys anywhere in an extension subtree, at any depth. These name a tool, an agent, a model, a permission, or a prompt, and a card that could set one would be choosing what the app runs rather than who the character is. The importer removes them; a conforming producer never writes them.

safeExtensionValue.description: Any JSON value, as long as no object anywhere inside it carries a privilege key. Nesting deeper than 16 levels is truncated on import.

openworkExtension.description: OpenWork's own block, written on export and applied on import. It is the only vendor namespace the importer keeps, so it is the only place these values survive a round trip. Everything in it is re-normalized on the way in — flattened to single lines, capped, and given fresh ids where needed — because the sanitizer bounds a card's size and strips privilege keys from vendor blocks but does not cap the length or the count of anything inside one.

version.description: This block's shape, versioned separately from the card spec so it can change without claiming to be a new card format. Recorded on import but not yet branched on.

nsfw.description: Whether this character tracks explicit scene state. Applied on import, so a shared character arrives configured the way its author built it. The character editor shows it before the character is saved.

hardLimits.description: Content this character must never produce. Applied on import. Entries are flattened to single lines, capped, de-duplicated, and empties dropped; a list longer than the cap is truncated. Note that a card which can write this list can also ship a shorter one than the importer would have chosen, which is why the editor shows it before the character is saved.

sceneRecords.description: The scene a session opens with, in the order the scene acquires them. Order is meaningful: it survives into the compiled prompt within each type. Applied on import, after the same normalization the app applies to its own records.

attachedSkills.description: Never read on import, whatever a card puts here. A skill ref names a file in the importing workspace, which the card knows nothing about; letting it choose one would let it choose what writing guidance the character runs under.

sceneRecord.description: One tracked thing in a scene. `state` and `count` coexist rather than forming a union: a garment usually wants no count, a counter usually wants no state, and a record that wants both costs nothing.

id.description: Unique within the card. The model addresses records by this id for the whole conversation, so an id is never reused and never reassigned by a rename. On import a missing or duplicated id is replaced with a freshly minted one rather than honoured, so a card cannot choose an id that collides with one the model is given later.

type.description: An open slug set, not an enum. `clothes`, `pose`, `location`, `climax`, `body_parts` and `toys` are rendered with known labels and in that order; anything else matching the pattern is accepted and rendered in a trailing group. Bounded on both ends because it becomes a heading in the system prompt. A record's type is fixed once created.

name.description: The specific thing: "silk blouse", "left wrist". Empty for singletons like pose or location. The ceiling bounds the store, not the prompt; the prompt budget is applied when the scene section is rendered.

state.description: Free text: "worn", "removed", "kneeling on the rug". Flattened to a single line and stripped of heading markers on the way in, because it is re-injected into the system message on every later turn.

count.description: For records that count. Absent, not zero, for records that do not — a labelled empty value invites the model to fill it in for the sake of the label.

description.description: Authored detail the prompt may use. Trimmed to a preview, and then dropped entirely, before any record is shed for budget.
